newsitem.title: USA: Weekend heat in Iowa welcomed, crop growth slow.
newsitem.headline: Weekend heat in Iowa welcomed, crop growth slow.

text.p: Warmer temperatures over the weekend ended June 1 were welcomed by Iowa farmers who have reported slow early crop growth, the state's weekly agricultural statistics service report said.
Temperatures for the week as a whole averaged six to nine degrees below normal, but warmer weather was seen over the weekend, the report said.
The state's cooler-than-normal temperatures have caused yellow corn leaves, slow soybean emergence and short hay fields, farmers surveyed by the state agency said.
Emergence of corn seedlings occurred on 87 percent of acreage, two days of ahead of last year's pace and one week ahead of the five-year average.
Soybeans were 92 percent planted versus 58 last year and the 69 percent average, while emergence at 45 percent was also about one week ahead of last year and three days ahead of average.
Oats condition declined slightly, with the crop rated 63 percent good to excellent, 31 percent fair and six percent poor to very poor.
Winter wheat condition declined with the crop rated 67 percent good to excellent, 29 percent fair, four percent poor and one percent very poor.
Pasture conditions declined as well and were rated seven percent excellent, 39 good, 41 fair, and 11 poor as of Sunday.
Topsoil moisture as of Friday, May 30 was rated 19 percent surplus, 78 adequate, and 3 short.
